name: Health Screening Without Specialists
deck: AI is absorbing the cultural authority of human experts—from customer service to underwriting to creative work—and the platforms that own the AI layer are capturing the economic relationship formerly held by intermediaries. In healthcare, this means diagnostic screening is shifting from credentialed specialists to autonomous mail-in testing systems.
core_bet: AI capability has crossed the threshold where it can perform judgment-level work at scale and sufficient quality to replace human intermediaries without hiring the professionals. This is not efficiency gain alone; it is a transfer of trust and economic authority from credentialed humans to algorithm-owning platforms. The intermediary—the doctor, the specialist, the advisor—is being repositioned as a legacy service or luxury good.

numbers.airbnb_ai_resolution_rate: 45% of customer issues resolved without human agent (Q2 2026)
numbers.airbnb_support_cost_decline: 16% year-over-year reduction in cost per booking

mechanism: AI systems trained on expert decisions reproduce that logic at machine speed, eliminating the need for human intermediaries. Exact Sciences' Cologuard removes the gastroenterologist from the screening pathway by making cancer detection mail-in and autonomous. The patient relationship shifts from professional guidance to platform convenience. Platforms that own the AI layer capture three forms of value: operational savings from reduced headcount, pricing power by absorbing what experts charged separately, and proprietary data from the billions of decisions their systems make. Exact Sciences keeps the screening revenue; the patient never speaks to a specialist.
why_now: AI capability crossed the threshold in 2024-2026 where it can perform judgment tasks with sufficient reliability for mass-market deployment. LLMs and domain-specific models can now handle diagnostic screening, customer support, and underwriting at a quality level acceptable to consumers and regulators. At the same time, labor costs, liability concerns, and competitive pressure to reduce cost per unit all created economic urgency to swap humans for AI systems. The confluence of capability and incentive is creating a rapid reordering of who holds expertise and who can charge for it.
who_pays: Customer service agents, financial advisors, diagnostic specialists, credentialed healthcare providers whose expertise can be encoded into training data and then replaced by a machine. These are middle-class knowledge workers—radiologists, underwriters, specialists, doctors—whose professional authority and pricing power is being absorbed into platform algorithms. Patients who lose the option of human guidance and recourse. Healthcare systems that no longer employ screening specialists because mail-in testing is cheaper.
who_profits: Platform operators that own the AI layer: Exact Sciences (screening access through mail-in testing), Affirm (credit underwriting via AdaptAI and BoostAI), Airbnb (customer service and discovery), Stagwell (creative and workflow automation), Shopify (merchant discovery and commerce), American Express (payment routing and transaction data). These companies monetize the efficiency gain while also capturing the relationship and data that experts previously held.
tension: AI intermediaries trained on existing human decisions reproduce and amplify existing biases, make errors at scale rather than individually, and strip accountability from outcomes. When an AI misses a cancer diagnosis, the question of who is liable, who takes responsibility, and who the affected person can appeal to has no clear answer. Removing the human intermediary removes a friction point that previously allowed for exceptions, negotiation, and judgment calls based on context. The platform's scale efficiency comes at the cost of human agency and recourse.
surprising_part: AI disintermediation is not limited to customer service work that was already struggling. It is happening simultaneously across healthcare (Exact Sciences), financial services (Affirm), and hospitality (Airbnb). What connects them is that human intermediaries were not primarily valued for their labor cost; they were valued for their perceived expertise, judgment, and trust. Once AI systems can credibly perform those functions, the cultural relationship flips. The intermediary becomes legacy infrastructure rather than irreplaceable expertise.
one_sentence: When platforms absorb the cultural authority of experts and make their judgment proprietary to algorithms, the people who held that authority become optional, while the platforms that own the AI layer capture the economic relationship forever.
societal_stake: As AI absorbs the functions of doctors, financial advisors, and creative professionals across healthcare, finance, and creative work, the professions that gave the middle class access to expertise become either luxury goods—human access for those who can pay premium fees—or AI-mediated services for everyone else. The cultural authority previously held by credentialed humans transfers irreversibly to algorithm-owning platforms. When all screening is mail-in, all credit is algorithmically determined, and all customer problems are AI-resolved, human expertise no longer commands its own price. It becomes embedded in platform services.

evidence.exact_sciences: Cologuard mail-in stool DNA test removes the colonoscopy and the gastroenterologist from the colorectal cancer screening pathway; FY2025 revenue $3.25B with screening more people than ever through autonomous testing
evidence.airbnb: Nearly 45% of customer issues beginning with AI assistant were resolved without human agent in Q2 2026; customer-support cost per booking declined ~16% year-over-year
evidence.affirm: Q3 2026 net income $100M on $1.039B revenue with adjusted operating income 27%; AdaptAI and BoostAI optimize financing-offer selection and merchant program design
evidence.stagwell: The Marketing Cloud delivered 230% YoY revenue growth; record net new business $171M in Q2 2026; positioned as core agentic applications for marketing replacing traditional agencies
evidence.american_express: FY2025 revenue $72.2B with net income $10.8B; annual narrative explicitly frames AI-powered agents discovering products, making decisions, and completing payments as AmEx positioning to be embedded in agentic transaction flow
evidence.shopify: Q2 2026 GMV reached $115.6B with Shopify Payments penetration at 68% ($78.1B); positioning Catalog and Sidekick for AI-agent commerce discovery and merchant automation
